questions.question: Palm-leaf manuscripts. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Palm- leaf manuscripts-made out of dried palm leaves- used to recording royal edicts, temple
  • records, land grants, literature, and religious texts- written mainly in Malayalam, Tamil, or
  • Sanskrit- vital historical sources that reveal Kerala’s administration, culture, and knowledge
  • system

questions.question: Pattanam. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Pattanam - Located near North Paravur in Ernakulam district- important archaeological site in
  • pre-modern Kerala- believed to be the ancient port of Muziris (Muchiri), a major centre of Indo-
  • Roman trade mentioned in Sangam literature and Greco-Roman writings.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Megalith. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Megalith- Mega means large and lithos means stone-Megalith means large stone monuments-
  • used for burial purposes - Common types include dolmens, cists, umbrella stones (Kodakkal) etc.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Karalar. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Karalar- landholders or local chieftains- controlled and managed agricultural lands- they played
  • an important role in the village administration and agrarian system.

questions.question: Koyiladhikarikal. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Koyiladhikarikal- temple authorities or officials who managed the affairs of temples- responsible

questions.solution_html:
• Vaishnavism - developed along with the Bhakti movement- worshipped Lord Vishnu and his

questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Perumals Decline. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Perumals Decline- internal conflicts, rise of powerful local chieftains (Naduvazhis), and the
  • weakening of central authority - growing independence of temple authorities and Brahmin
  • settlements (Brahmadeyams) also reduced royal control.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Arunnattuvar. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Arunnattuvar – temple management authorities during the Brahmin supremacy in Kerala - local
  • administrative officers or officials who worked under the Perumals or Naduvazhis (local
  • chieftains)

• Purayitam- low-lying agricultural land or wetland used mainly for paddy cultivation- household
  • and agricultural land together in a place.

questions.question: Discuss the literary sources on the history of Kerala ? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the literary sources on the history of Kerala - Sangam literature -earliest reference
  • to Chera kings and trade-Keralolpathi -origin legend of Kerala and Brahmin settlements -
  • Unnuneelisandesam and Manipravalam poems - Temple inscriptions and copper plates record land
  • grants- Foreign accounts -Travelogues by Ibn Battuta and Duarte Barbosa.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyze the level of technological and architectural skill required to create the different types of megaliths in Kerala? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the level of technological and architectural skill required to create the different
  • types of megaliths in Kerala- Cists, Dolmens, Urns, Menhirs, Rock-Cut Tombs- Accurate stone
  • cutting and shaping without iron tools- Alignment and orientation show planning skill-
  • Underground chambers need engineering knowledge-Transportation of large slabs shows
  • organized labor-Burial goods reflect metal-working and craft skills- Regional variation indicates
  • experimentation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the evolution of tenurial relations in ancient Kerala.? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the evolution of tenurial relations in ancient Kerala- Early communal land
  • ownership under clan chiefs- Gradual privatization with settled agriculture-
  • Rise of Brahmadeyam villages -Devaswam lands- Janmi–Kanam system-Agrarian hierarchy
  • became rigidly caste-based-Tenurial system supported temple economy-Continued influence till
  • colonial land reforms.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the role of Nadu-level institutions in integrating agriculture with polity and society.? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the role of Nadu-level institutions in integrating agriculture with polity and
  • society-Nadu -cluster of villages forming a political unit- Headed by Naduvazhi or local chief-
  • Coordination of agricultural activities and irrigation-Supervised tax collection and land
  • distribution-Ur-Temples acted as economic centers- Political, social, and economic life
  • interconnected-Maintained local law and order-Strengthened regional identity and state formation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the role of fishing and hunting in Tinai economy.? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of fishing and hunting in Tinai economy-Ecological region-Neytal Tinai-
  • coastal zone dependent on fishing- Palai-Mullai-hunting and gathering activities-Provided protein
  • and trade commodities -Fish, Meat-Subsistence base for non-agricultural groups-Seasonal
  • occupation tied to nature cycles-Cultural rituals linked with sea and forest deities-Supported
  • maritime trade through fish exports- ecological adaptation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the role of major ports like Muziris and Kollam in overseas trade of premodern Kerala. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of major ports like Muziris and Kollam in overseas trade of premodern
  • Kerala-Muziris -major port of ancient Cheras-Linked Kerala with Rome, Arabia, and Egypt-
  • Exported pepper, pearls, ivory, timber- Imported gold, wine, glass, and textiles-Kollam -After
  • Muziris decline- Center of Arab, Chinese, and Southeast Asian trade- Brought wealth and
  • cosmopolitan culture.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the early spread of Islam through Arab traders on the Malabar coast. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the early spread of Islam through Arab traders on the Malabar coast-Pre-existing
  • Arab trade contacts before Islam-Muslim traders arrived by 7th century CE- Peaceful propagation
  • through commerce-Cheraman Juma Masjid- Local rulers welcomed Arab settlers-Inter-marriages
  • with local women-Mappila Muslim community-Mosques became centers of faith and trade-Islam
  • integrated into Kerala’s plural society.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine the relationship between the Swaroopams and the powerful Nair aristocracy. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the relationship between the Swaroopams and the powerful Nair aristocracy-
  • Ruling lineage-royal house-Perumpadappu, Nediyiruppu, Venad-Nairs formed military and
  • administrative class-Hereditary service ties between kings and Nairs- Nairs controlled local
  • governance and defense-Received land and titles for service- Maintained caste and political order-
  • Basis of Kerala’s feudal political system.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyze the role of powerful local rulers in both facilitating and regulating trade. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the role of powerful local rulers in both facilitating and regulating trade-Chera,
  • Zamorin, Venad kings-patronized trade-Maintained port facilities and customs offices-protection
  • to merchants and ships- copper plates-Anjuvannam, Manigramam-Ports became centres of urban
  • growth-Controlled trade ensured both profit and stability.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How did caste-based occupations affect the social status of men and women in pre-modern Kerala? / [CO3] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• How did caste-based occupations affect the social status of men and women in pre-modern
  • Kerala- Occupation determined by hereditary caste-Brahmins-ritual and land control- Nairs -
  • military and administrative duties-Artisan and service castes - productive labor- Lower castes –
  • agriculture, fishing, manual work Occupation defined purity–pollution hierarchy- strict social
  • rules-Women’s roles confined within caste norms-Economic inequality reflected in social ranking-
  • Caste occupation reinforced rigid social structure.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the influence of Kerala’s topography on its human settlements. ? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the influence of Kerala’s topography on its human settlements. Narrow coastal
  • strip – The long coastline encouraged fishing, trade, and port-based settlements (like Muziris,
  • Kollam, Kozhikode)- Western Ghats barrier – The mountain ranges limited inland expansion but
  • provided spices, forest products, and protection from invasions-Rivers and backwaters –
  • Numerous rivers and waterways supported agriculture, transport, and dense settlements in fertile
  • valleys-Fertile plains – The midland and coastal plains enabled wet-rice cultivation, leading to
  • clustered agrarian villages-Highland and forest zones – Sparsely populated; inhabited mainly by
  • Adivasi and tribal communities engaged in shifting cultivation and hunting-Climate and rainfall –
  • Heavy monsoons shaped housing styles (sloped roofs, raised platforms) and seasonal agricultural
  • patterns.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Assess how caste formation and regional identity were shaped by monarchical and Brahminical dominance in early Kerala.? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Assess how caste formation and regional identity were shaped by monarchichal and
  • brahmanical dominance in early kerala. - Monarchical rise – Local chieftains (naduvazhis,
  • desavazhis) and Chera rulers built hierarchical polities seeking ritual legitimacy-Brahmin
  • migration – Arrival of Namboothiri Brahmins (7th–9th c. CE) introduced varna ideology to
  • Kerala-Temple centered economy – Kings granted brahmadeyam lands to Brahmins, making
  • temples economic and social hubs – Mutual support: kings gained divine authority, Brahmins
  • gained land and power-Caste formation – Society structured into rigid hierarchy: Brahmins,
  • Nairs/Kshatriyas, Ezhavas, Pulayas, etc - Ritual purity & pollution – Unique Kerala system of
  • untouchability and unapproachability reinforced caste divisions. Land control – Brahmins and
  • elites-controlled land; lower castes tied to agrarian labor and servitude– Local deities and customs
  • merged with Brahmanical worship, shaping a distinct regional culture-Language & identity
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyze the role of temples as centers of redistribution and economic integration. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse the role of temples as centers of redistribution and economic integration-Land
  • grants (Devadana/Brahmadeyam) – Temples owned vast lands donated by kings and elites-
  • Agrarian control – Managed cultivation, collected produce, and organized local labour-
  • Redistribution of wealth – Distributed grains, wages, and offerings to priests, workers, and poor-
  • Employment hub – Provided work to priests, artisans, dancers, cleaners, guards, etc-Temple
  • economy – Functioned as centres of production, storage, and exchange-Market growth –
  • Stimulated local trade and craft industries around temple towns -Social integration – Linked
  • different castes, occupations, and regions through shared economic activity– Temples reflected
  • royal patronage and helped integrate local polities -Cultural centre – Promoted art, music, and
  • education, uniting society through religion and economy.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Critically analyze the trial and ordeal system as a reflection of the socio- religious life in medieval Kerala. / [CO4] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Critically analyse the trial and ordeal system as a reflection of socio-religious life in
  • medieval Kerala. Types of ordeals – Common methods included fire ordeal (Thee-divyam),
  • water ordeal (Jala-divyam), poison test, and touching sacred objects to prove truthfulness-
  • Brahmanical influence – Brahmins often conducted and supervised ordeals, linking justice with
  • ritual purity and Vedic authority-Social hierarchy – The system favoured upper castes who had
  • access to temple rituals; lower castes faced harsher or humiliating ordeals-Gender dimension –
  • Women, especially in cases of adultery or chastity, were often subjected to trial by fire or water,
  • showing patriarchal bias-Absence of rational evidence – Judgments depended on faith and ritual,
  • not on factual or legal reasoning — showing a pre-modern moral order-Reflection of socio-
  • religious life – Reveals how law, religion, and caste were deeply intertwined; justice was seen as a
  • sacred, not secular, process-Critical view – Though it reflected religious faith and social order, it
  • also reinforced inequality, superstition, and priestly dominance, eventually replaced by rational
  • legal systems under colonial rule.
  • [2x10 = 20]
